newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary president approves ouster of minister.
newsitem.headline: Hungary president approves ouster of minister.

text.p: Hungarian President Arpad Goncz has relieved industry and trade minister Tamas Suchman of his post on the recommendation of the prime minister, the Hungarian news agency said on Tuesday.
Suchman will leave office on Wednesday, the MTI news agency added.

Prime Minister Gyula Horn recommended on October 6 that Suchman be sacked after it was made public that the state privatisation agency APV Rt, which Suchman oversaw, illegally awarded a contract to a consultant which netted her fees amounting to more than 800 million forints ($5.2 million). @
The executive and advisory boards of APV also were sacked in the biggest scandal to hit the socialist-led government since it took office in 1994.
Suchman has denied any wrongdoing but the scandal has caused a serious rift in the ruling coalition made up of Horn's Hungarian Socialist Party and the Free Democrats.
A meeting of the ruling coalition's coordination council has been called for Wednesday morning, MTI said. @

Horn has nominated Judit Csiha, a political state secretary at the Justice Ministry, to succeed Suchman as privatisation minister. Horn nominated Szabolcs Fazakas, Hungary's ambassador to Germany, to be minister of industry, trade and tourism.
